items.excerpt: ## Democrats’ Senate Majority Expands to 55 as Scott Colom Claims Historic Win in Mississippi Nov 12, 2026 Scott Colom has made history as Mississippi’s first Democratic senator since 1982 — and its first African American senator since the post-Civil War Reconstruction era. Colom narrowly defeated Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, who conceded defeat in a video posted on social media Wednesday afternoon. Hours later, Colom addressed supporters at a victory party at the historically Black Tougaloo College in Jackson. > Sen.-elect Scott Colom: “For months and months, I’ve been telling everybody, everywhere I go, that we’re going to win this election. … But every time I said it, I pointed out that people were going to give me too much credit for it, because it’s not something that I did, y’all. It’s something that we did.” Scott Colom’s victory brings the incoming Senate Democratic caucus to 55, with Alaska’s race still too close to call. On Wednesday, Democrat Mary Peltola expanded her narrow lead over incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, with about 15% of ballots left to be counted. Meanwhile, Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins is leading in Alaska’s governor’s race. ... ## Israeli Strike on Nasser Hospital in Gaza Kills at Least Six People Including Surgeon Nov 12, 2026 In Gaza, an Israeli strike on a building at Nasser Hospital killed at least six people and wounded 20 others today. A surgeon, Dr. Rizo Abu Shaira, who was featured in the documentary “American Doctor,” was killed in the strike. Footag ... Injured patients were moved on stretchers through hallways covered in rubble. This is a doctor, Ayman Abu Obeid. ... A Hamas spokesperson condemned the strike as a “fully-fledged war crime.” Since last October’s so-called ceasefire, at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks. ... ## Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns In breaking news, Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang has resigned. This follows reports that Nvidia’s board of directors was preparing to remove him after an internal investigation into his affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence officials claim was spying for Beijing. Huang was reportedly the target of a Chinese intelligence operation that attempted to convince him to lobby U.S. officials to allow the export of advanced computer chips to China. ... ## Millions Take Part in General Strike in Spain In Spain, millions of people took to the streets for the first general strike in 14 years to protest against rising housing costs and stagnant wages. Tenants’ associations and unions led the protests with a 24-hour work stoppage. The protests come less than three weeks before a snap general election.

items.title: National and International News in Focus: Nov. 12 | National | wktv.com
items.excerpt: ## Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after his affair raises national security concerns Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is resigning after his affair raises national security concerns. The company named Colette Kress as interim CEO on Thursday. She is the current executive vice president and chief financial officer. Huang faced growing calls to resign after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Late Wednesday, media reports said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reported to him. Shares of Nvidia, one of the largest companies in the world, plunged 10% in premarket trading Thursday. ## 5 people are shot in a trendy DC neighborhood, including 1 killed at a gym, a witness says WASHINGTON (AP) — Authorities say five people have been shot in a trendy Washington, D.C., neighborhood within walking distance of the White House. A witness says at least one of those shot was at a gym and died. Police say a shooting suspect was barricaded Thursday near the initial shooting site. The shootings were reported in Logan Circle, a mile north of the White House. The area includes a VIDA fitness center, St. Luke’s Episcopal Church, residences and a Whole Foods supermarket. Witness James Spellman was at the gym when he heard shots fired. Spellman says a man was shot in the neck, fell to the ground and died in a pool of blood. ## US envoys meet with Putin in Moscow on Ukraine talks, then head for Dublin to see Zelenskyy MOSCOW (AP) — U.S. envoys held talks about the fighting in Ukraine with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin. The meeting, which lasted about two hours on Thursday, follows U.S.-mediated negotiations between Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi. The talks resulted in an agreement on a large prisoner exchange, though no breakthrough was made in ending the nearly 5-year-old conflict. The U.S. envoys aim to involve Europe in negotiations, but Moscow is resistant. They will now head to Dublin, Ireland, to brief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. He sees a political opportunity for peace due to changes in the U.S. Congress and upcoming elections in Europe. Meanwhile, fighting continues, and Ukraine faces new disruptions in its Starlink internet service. ... ## Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills 6 people, including a doctor and a child, Health Ministry says KHAN YOUNIS, Gaza Strip (AP) — Gaza’s Health Ministry says an Israeli airstrike has hit one of the main hospitals still operating in the Gaza Strip, killing six people, including a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy. The Israeli military said the strike Thursday on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza was targeting a Hamas commander and other militants, without providing evidence. The commander it identified was not among the dead. The ministry and witnesses said the strike hit the hospital’s surgical wing. Footage showed several wards and operating rooms heavily damaged or destroyed, with debris scattered across hospital beds and equipment and rebar dangling from holes in the ceiling. At least 28 people were wounded. ## Death toll rises to 8 in Brooklyn building collapse as rescuers dig through rubble NEW YORK (AP) — At least eight people have died after a three-story building in Brooklyn collapsed at the edge of a construction site. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the death toll Thursday morning as firefighters continued to dig through the rubble in the search for others. The building, adjacent to a construction site, collapsed on Wednesday afternoon. Rescuers worked overnight, using dogs to sniff for survivors. The cause of the collapse is under investigation. The three-story building was a mixed-use structure with apartments above commercial space. Mamdani says at least 17 people have been injured, including three firefighters. ## Pope Leo returns to a national celebration in his second homeland of Peru LIMA, Peru (AP) — Pope Leo XIV has declared Peru his “homeland” as he arrived in Lima Wednesday at the start of his historic visit. Leo credits Peruvians with having formed him as a pastor by sharing their lives, joys and struggles with him. A nationwide party erupted to welcome the country's beloved “Padre Robert” home. The visit to Peru marks the final leg of Leo’s three-nation South America tour.

items.title: Stubborn inflation raises prospect of more aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes
items.excerpt: The big picture: Measures designed to strip out unusually large price swings suggest that underlying inflation pressures are gaining pace. - The Cleveland Fed's trimmed-mean Consumer Price Index —which filters out unusually large price swings to give a clearer picture of underlying inflation — rose 0.4% in October, the largest monthly increase since May. - The Atlanta Fed's sticky-price CPI, which tracks prices that typically change, slowly accelerated to a 4.7% annualized pace in October, its fastest since February 2025. - More than three-quarters of the consumer price basket saw prices rise at an annualized rate exceeding 2% in October, the largest share since August 2022, Charles Schwab's head of macro research Kevin Gordon posted on X. Yes, but: The Fed may have reason to proceed cautiously even against the backdrop of stubborn inflation. - Rising bond yields and a sell-off in technology stocks (revived again by the exit of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang) are already tightening financial conditions — potentially doing some of the work of higher interest rates. - Fed governor Michelle Bowman said in a speech that falling stock prices, higher borrowing costs and a stronger dollar could weigh on economic growth, particularly in sectors already struggling with high interest rates. - Cleveland Fed president Beth Hammack, who dissented against the decision to hold rates steady last month, said she still supported a more gradual approach to raising rates. "It's less disruptive to the overall economy than moving in sharper, more aggressive movements," she said Thursday morning.

items.title: As Higher Prices Seep into Broader Economy, Fed Officials Consider Faster Hikes | Industrial Distribution
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON (AP) — More evidence this week of hot inflation in the U.S. was unpleasant news for the Federal Reserve, not to mention consumers: Rising prices may be spreading beyond the one-time shocks from tariffs and high gas prices into the wider economy, meaning that mortgages, credit cards and other forms of borrowing are likely to become increasingly expensive. Tuesday's consumer price index report showed broadly rising costs across a range of goods and services, some with little connection to more expensive oil and gas or surging investment in artificial intelligence data centers, another factor blamed for worsening inflation. And there is increasing anxiety among Fed officials that higher oil prices stemming from the Iran war may last longer than previously thought. A key issue debated by Fed policymakers for months has been whether inflation would cool on its own if the Iran war ended and oil prices fell and as the impact of tariffs faded. But government data suggested inflation rose to 4% in October compared with a year ago, up from 3.7% in September, even as gas prices leveled off. The potential consequences of the new inflation data emerged immediately. Two Fed officials suggested Tuesday that the central bank may have to hike its key interest rate more quickly to tame inflation. Bigger or faster hikes by the Fed would mean that buying a house or a car, or paying off a credit card would become a steeper hill to climb, with millions of Americans already struggling to make ends meet. Lorie Logan, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas and a voting member of the Fed's rate-setting committee, said Tuesday that price increases remain high for services such as "visits to the doctor, childcare, dining out and hotel stays." "Prices for these services aren't particularly sensitive to tariffs, conflict in the Middle East or surging demand for computer chips," she added. "While I expect inflation to moderate as price pressures dissipate in energy and manufactured goods, the broader inflationary trend is more likely to persist." Logan said Tuesday she supported two additional quarter-point rate hikes. While she has made similar statements before, Logan added that the Fed could "move more rapidly this winter" than it "has moved so far this fall," signaling that she may support two rate hikes in a row, a quicker pace than the Fed's current approach. ... Wall Street investors now see 90% odds that the Fed will lift borrowing costs at its next meeting Dec. 8-9, according to futures prices tracked by CME Fedwatch. ... Tuesday's inflation report showed prices rising in many areas with little connection to energy costs or AI, including streaming video services, beef and auto insurance. But surging investment in data centers has driven up the cost of computer chips, power generation equipment, and copper, among other components, with little sign of easing. items.title: Up First briefing: Scott Colom; Trump; Russia-Ukraine talks; El-Sayed : NPR
items.excerpt: Democrat Scott Colom has won the U.S. Senate seat from Mississippi, defeating Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by just a few thousand votes. Colom will be the first Black Senator from the state in nearly 150 years. His win expands the Democratic majority in the new Congress to 55 seats. The Alaska race is still undecided. ... - 🎧 Colom's win highlights growing voter concerns about affordability and the impact of the war in Iran, Elise Catrion Gregg of the Gulf States Newsroom and Mississippi Public Broadcasting tells Up First. During her campaign, Hyde-Smith relied on her record and President Trump's support, which Gregg says is no longer a winning strategy. This race signals a potential national shift, showing that the South is becoming a viable target for Democrats, Gregg says. - ➡️ A U.S. Supreme Court ruling this year weakened the Voting Rights Act, raising the possibility of a record drop in Black Congressional representation. The Democratic blue wave lessened the expected decline, but an NPR analysis shows that Black representation in the U.S. House is still slated to decrease with the incoming Congress. The White House is warning Democrats that their planned investigations into administration officials could cross the line into "blatant criminality." White House Counsel Will Scharf said in a letter to Rep. Robert Garcia, who is expected to lead the House Oversight Committee next year, that the administration is monitoring "abusive and capricious threats" from Democrats. The letter concludes by saying that "the administration will not be extorted and will not be cowed by unlawful process, motivated by animus, pettiness, hatred or any other unlawful motive to intimidate, penalize or interfere with the lawful functioning of government." Garcia said Democrats will not be deterred by threats from the Department of Justice or Trump's lawyers. - 🎧 The administration's arguments may buy time and push Democrats to go to court to enforce their subpoenas, NPR's Tamara Keith says. She adds that the White House letter gives a preview of the legal arguments the administration might use next year. But more importantly, Keith says that it signals that the White House and Justice Department won't accept congressional investigations and oversight without a fight. Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a significant prisoner swap after two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi. Trump's envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are now in Moscow today to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and attempt to make more headway to end the war in Ukraine. - 🎧 NPR's Charles Maynes says that, going into the talks in Abu Dhabi, U.S. officials were exploring Article 5-like guarantees for Ukraine, similar to NATO's collective security defense. A move like this would be significant if implemented, but Moscow has already rejected the concept of a "NATO lite" status for Ukraine and its full NATO membership. Kushner said that, in Moscow, he aims to brief Putin directly and persuade him to involve Europeans in discussions about European security.

Artists like Elvis Costello, Sheryl Crow and Emmylou Harris performed his songs Wednesday night at the Troubadour club in Los Angeles. Jurors found that Yella Beezy hired the gunman who fatally shot rapper MO3. Yella Beezy’s real name is Markies Conway, and MO3’s real name was Melvin Noble. items.title: Arnold Vosloo Confirms Imhotep Returns in The Mummy: Book of the Dead | Movieversalfilm
items.excerpt: ### Arnold Vosloo confirms Imhotep is back for The Mummy: Book of the Dead ... - What’s new: Arnold Vosloo has signed to play the high priest Imhotep again, his first time in the role since The Mummy Returns in 2001. He confirmed it on Jack Carr’s Danger Close podcast, FANGORIA reported - What he said: Vosloo said Brendan Fraser and the cast are already shooting in London, that he heads there this month, and that the script is “very good”. He also gave away the first plot hint: someone reads from the Book of the Dead and brings Imhotep back to life - Who’s making it: Radio Silence (Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett) direct. Rachel Weisz, John Hannah, Oded Fehr and Kevin J. O’Connor also return, and the film is a direct sequel to The Mummy Returns - UK availability: UK date not yet confirmed. It opens in US cinemas on 15 October 2027 ... - What’s new: Don Mancini, who created Chucky in 1988’s Child’s Play and has written every film in his series, has signed with Independent Artist Group, where he will focus on developing the next Chucky film alongside new original film and TV projects, Deadline reported - The plan: Bloody Disgusting adds that Mancini is set to write and direct the new film, which is aimed at cinemas, would keep the continuity of the films and the three-season Chucky TV series, and aims to make the killer doll scary again ... ### Curzon brings Jodie Comer’s body horror musical Stuffed to UK cinemas ... - What’s new: Curzon has bought Stuffed, UK filmmaker Theo Rhys’s debut feature, for the UK and Ireland after its world premiere opened the Discovery section at Toronto, Screen International reported - The story: Jodie Comer plays Araminta, a reclusive taxidermist who advertises for the perfect human specimen to stuff, and Harry Melling plays Bernie, a lonely factory worker who answers because he fears leaving no legacy. As their macabre plan takes shape, a romance grows between them - Who’s making it: Joss Holden-Rea co-wrote the script and composed the songs. It grows out of Rhys’s BAFTA-nominated short of the same name and was developed by the BFI - UK availability: Coming to UK and Irish cinemas through Curzon; UK date not yet confirmed
